solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rotate one vegetable, so to speak, for another

parts.note: to rotate is to turn
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: signals that the word pea is used only for its sound, the letter name P

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A cook's instruction to swap one vegetable for a different one on a crop rotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is short for another vegetable: the answer is a second vegetable, built from TURN, I and the letter P, which sounds like 'pea' ('so to speak').
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a root crop, so it is a different vegetable from the pea in the wordplay.

clue.text: Article revised Rome's established principles

parts.note: the definite article is THE

indicators.note: something revised has been altered, so the letters of Rome's are rearranged

explanation.surface: An article has been rewritten to restate Rome's settled doctrines.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorems are propositions proved and accepted, so they are settled principles in mathematics or logic.

clue.text: Fleet seizing power in sudden attack

indicators.note: the raid grabs hold of the power letter, so it sits inside

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A naval fleet takes control of a power station in a surprise raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' reads as a group of ships, but here it is the adjective meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, fleet means swift or quick on the feet, a synonym of very fast.

clue.text: Ordains after conversion — that's progress

indicators.note: once converted, the word ordains has its letters changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A church ordaining people after they convert counts as headway for the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To make inroads is to advance into new territory, so the word is a synonym for headway.

clue.text: Bird started eating tasty morsel

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
bit, as in took a bite of, describes starting to eat something

explanation.surface: A bird begins pecking at a delicious scrap of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small choice piece of food, a delicacy.

clue.text: Actually accepting right to break law, say

indicators.note: the phrase in fact takes in the letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: in fact means actually

explanation.surface: Someone admits that, in truth, they claim a right to break the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the law as just one example of a rule that can be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To infract is a rare verb meaning to infringe or violate a rule or statute.

clue.text: Practical joke producing disapproval by some when upset

parts.note: boo is a cry of disapproval

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset turns a word upside down, so part is read in reverse

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: A prank draws boos from some people when they are upset by it.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a hidden prank set up to catch someone out, a kind of hoax or jape.

clue.text: Religious faith is embraced by people opposed to us

indicators.note: the word is is held inside the other word, as in a hug

parts.note: them, as in us and them, are the people on the other side

explanation.surface: A faith is welcomed even by the people who oppose us.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods, a religious creed.

clue.text: Move forwards with support of backs in game

definitions.text: Move forwards with support of backs in game

parts.words: Move forwards with support of backs in game
parts.note: in this playground game each player vaults ahead by pushing off the bent backs of others, which reads like rugby forwards and backs

explanation.walkthrough: 'forwards' and 'backs' suggest positions in rugby, but the game is the children's one of jumping over stooping players.
explanation.definitionFit: In the playground game players advance by vaulting over the bent backs of others; the verb also means to jump ahead.

clue.text: Honed lines for musicians — they should aim for perfect pitch

definitions.text: they should aim for perfect pitch

parts.note: a blade honed on a stone has been ground
the staff is the set of five lines on which music is written

explanation.surface: Musicians with sharpened skills read their lines, hoping for perfect pitch in the singing sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect pitch' looks musical; here it is a cricket or sports pitch, which these workers keep in perfect condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundstaff maintain sports grounds, so they want the playing surface in top condition.

clue.text: Fellow has to haul down flag, for example

parts.note: to lower something is to haul it down

explanation.surface: A man is told to take down a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' seems to be the thing being lowered, but it is the definition: a flag is a kind of iris.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag is a type of iris, a garden plant grown for its blooms, so it is one example.

clue.text: Raised money, as stated

indicators.note: stated means spoken, so the word is taken for how it sounds

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone has raised funds, so they claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bred is to have been brought up or reared, as children or livestock are.

clue.text: Revelation set back work in awful place, say

indicators.note: the reversed work is placed within the jumbled letters
something awful is a mess, so the letters of place and say are jumbled
set back means turned to face the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A revelation has pushed back some work in a dreadful location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual signal for an example or a sound-alike, but here it is part of the anagram fodder alongside 'place'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Revelation is also called by this Greek name, meaning an unveiling.

clue.text: Entertainer making many appearances?

parts.note: an entertainer who adopts many people's looks and voices; making appearances usually means turning up often

explanation.walkthrough: 'making many appearances' suggests a busy performer; read literally it is someone who puts on many different faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimic who copies the looks and voices of famous people on stage takes on many guises.

clue.text: Heading for India, perhaps, in seat arranged before spring

indicators.note: the anagram comes ahead of the word for spring
letters arranged in a new order are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: A traveller in an assigned seat leaves for India before spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling towards the east, which India is from Britain, means going in that direction.

clue.text: Poles switching places in ascent on railway — or descent

indicators.note: the poles are north and south, N and S; in the word ascent they trade positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Explorers on a railway climb, swapping one pole for the other, and then come back down.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the S and N of ASCENT gives ANCEST. The clue sets ascent against descent, with descent in the family-tree sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent means lineage or family origins, which is what ancestry describes.

clue.text: Avoidance behaviour that is seen in South Essex town

indicators.note: the Latin phrase appears inside the combination of south and the town

parts.note: Epping is a town in Essex, England
id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Evasive behaviour is a familiar sight in a town in south Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: ID EST is Latin for 'that is', usually seen as i.e. Epping is a market town in Essex, a county just east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidestepping a problem is dodging it, so the word describes evasive conduct.

clue.text: One who seeks satisfaction with a second helping

definitions.text: One who seeks satisfaction with a second helping

parts.words: One who seeks satisfaction with a second helping
parts.note: demanding satisfaction meant challenging to a fight, with a second as the assistant; it reads like a hungry diner wanting more

explanation.walkthrough: 'second helping' suggests more food; here the second is the friend who assists in an affair of honour, and satisfaction is the old idea of honour restored by fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter in a formal combat demanded satisfaction for an insult and was attended by a second.

clue.text: It helps one see clearly what's rubbish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lotion for rinsing the eyes

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses look connected, but one is a lotion and the other is slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a soothing lotion for the eyes and talk that is deceptive nonsense.

clue.text: Leader of party loathing speaker's position

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of party

parts.note: odium means hatred or loathing

explanation.surface: A party leader's dislike shapes the place a speaker holds in debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker's position' sounds like a stance in an argument; it is the raised platform a speaker stands on.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is the platform on which a speaker or conductor stands to address a crowd.

clue.text: Increase profit by 100%, producing delayed reaction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, to double the take, the takings
second meaning: a second look of surprise after a moment

explanation.walkthrough: The take is the money taken in, so doubling it is a 100% rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A double take is a second, startled look after failing to register something at first.

clue.text: Plane is one that's oddly targeted

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in the odd positions of targeted, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: An aircraft that has been singled out for attack, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft; it is the plane tree, common in London streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a broad-leaved species of the genus Platanus, so it is an example.

clue.text: In West End, I am performing Shakespearean title role

indicators.note: the end of west is its final letter

parts.note: contracted, I am is I'm
on, as in on stage, means performing

explanation.surface: An actor in London's West End says they are playing a Shakespeare lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district, but it means the last letter of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is the title character of a Shakespeare play about a misanthrope.

clue.text: Observance at heart of spiritualism

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle of the word spiritualism, inside it

explanation.surface: A ceremony lies at the centre of spiritualist practice.
explanation.definitionFit: An observance is a ceremony or rite kept regularly, which is what a ritual is.

clue.text: Person sharing quarters and uniform with ship's officer

parts.note: uniform as an adjective means even, level
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A sailor shares a cabin and a uniform with one of the ship's officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing but is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatmate is someone you share a rented home with, the British word for a roommate.

clue.text: Way one of our services can become trendy

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of Britain's armed services

explanation.surface: A way that one of the armed forces might become fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up to date and in fashion is current, the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: A number of sailors in third-class accommodation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sea song sung by sailors, a number being a song
second meaning: a crude hut or shack

explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a count of sailors but means a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a work song of seamen and a rough, poorly built dwelling.
